challengeTypes: identify: Which is HEAVIER — a book or a pencil? (Book vs Pencil vs Same)
identify: Which is LIGHTER — a feather or a stone? (Feather vs Stone vs Same)
identify: On a balance scale, which side goes DOWN? (The heavier side vs The lighter side vs Neither)
sort: Drag objects to heavy or light (Heavy: book, stone, iron ball | Light: feather, pencil, cotton ball)
identify: A big cotton ball and a small iron ball — which is heavier? (Iron ball vs Cotton ball vs Same)
identify: Can we tell weight just by looking at SIZE? (No, we need to compare with balance vs Yes, bigger is always heavier vs Yes, smaller is always lighter)
sort: Drag objects to the balance scale result (Goes down: heavy items | Goes up: light items | Same: equal weight items)
sort: Drag comparisons to correct or incorrect (Correct: stone heavier than feather, book heavier than pencil | Incorrect: feather heavier than stone, pencil heavier than book)
extraInstructions: IMPORTANT: Do NOT use speechManager.speak() anywhere in the game. Only use audioManager.play() for sound effects. Valid sound effects: pickup, drop-correct, drop-wrong, tap, success, error, celebration, hint. Teach: (1) Weight is how heavy or light something is. (2) A balance scale tips down on the heavier side. (3) Bigger does NOT always mean heavier — a small iron ball is heavier than a big cotton ball. (4) Always compare with the balance, not just by looking. Misconceptions: "bigger objects are always heavier" (big cotton ball is lighter than small iron ball), "same size = same weight" (coin and paper ball of same size weigh differently), "heavy means big" (small stone can be heavier than big feather). Default width=720, height=560. Use named export (export function BalanceGame), NOT export default. Export interface BalanceGameProps with width?, height?, onComplete?: (score: number) => void.
